items.entity: beam design domain (length x width x height)
items.description: Sec. 5.4 says only 'Given a design domain as illustrated in Figure 9(a)' and gives no size for the optimization domain. The only numbers are the printed specimen size, 120x48x48 mm^3, in the manufacturing paragraph. The text never says the optimization domain equals that box, or whether the beam has overhangs beyond the supports.
readings: Box 120 x 48 x 48 (L:W:H = 2.5:1:1), identical to the printed specimens
Box covering only the support span with a 48 x 48 cross-section (e.g. ~100 x 48 x 48), if the printed 120-mm beam includes overhangs

items.description: Fig. 9 caption: 'The bottom sides are fixed'. It does not say which part of the bottom is restrained (end edges, finite strips, inset lines, or lower parts of the end faces), how long the supported zones are, or whether they span the full width. The support span of the test rig is not given either.
readings: Full-width line supports on the two bottom end edges (x = 0 and x = L, z = 0)
Full-width bottom strips of finite length at each end (e.g. 0<=x<=0.05L and 0.95L<=x<=L, z = 0)
Full-width line supports set in from the ends at the rig span (e.g. x = 0.1L and x = 0.9L, z = 0)
Lower portions of the two end faces (x = 0 and x = L) restrained

items.description: The Fig. 9 caption calls the bottom sides 'fixed', which suggests clamping. But Sec. 5.4 and the Fig. 10(a) rig describe a physical three-point bending test, which normally uses simple (roller) supports. Which displacement components are restrained is not stated.
readings: Both supports fully clamped (ux = uy = uz = 0)
Both supports restrain only vertical displacement (rollers), plus minimal point constraints to remove rigid-body modes
One support pinned (all translations fixed), the other a roller (vertical, optionally lateral, only)

items.description: Fig. 9 caption: 'the force is uniformly applied at the center of the beam top'. The size and shape of the loaded region are not given (line across the width, patch, or point), nor whether it spans the full 48-mm width.
readings: Uniform line load across the full width at x = 0.5L on the top face
Uniform pressure on a full-width strip centred at mid-span (e.g. 0.45L-0.55L, or one element wide)
Uniform pressure on a small central patch of the top face (e.g. ~0.1L x 0.25W)
Concentrated point load at the centre of the top face

items.description: Neither Sec. 5.4 nor the Fig. 9 caption gives a force magnitude, total force or pressure.
readings: Unit total force (normalized)
Test-scale total force, e.g. 1 kN

items.description: Sec. 5.4 does not say whether any zones are fixed as solid or non-design, such as pads under the load or over the supports. Fig. 9(a) might show this but is unavailable. The porous model is only described as uniform before optimization.
readings: No passive regions; the whole box is designable
Solid (rho = rho_max) non-design pads beneath the load patch and above the supports

items.description: Sec. 4.3 uses the base-material tensor C*, but no values are given, and the additive-manufacturing material of the specimens is not named.
readings: E = 1 (normalized)
E ~ 2-3 GPa (typical AM photopolymer)
E ~ 110 GPa (Ti-6Al-4V)

items.description: Sec. 4.3 and Sec. 5.4 give no Poisson's ratio for the base material behind C* (and hence C^H).

items.entity: effective (homogenized) stiffness-density law of the porous unit
items.description: Sec. 4.3 (Eq. 26) gives only the form c_ij(rho)/c*_ij = a1*exp(a2*rho) - a1 for an orthotropic C^H with 9 independent constants. The fitted a1 and a2 for the units of Table 2(a)/(c) are not reported; curves appear only in Fig. 4(b), for an unidentified symmetric unit. How the unit axes line up with the beam is not stated. A single-material solver needs an equivalent interpolation.
readings: Paper's exponential law with orthotropic C^H, coefficients read from Fig. 4(b)
Isotropic SIMP E(rho) = rho^3 * E0
Isotropic Gibson-Ashby-type power law E(rho) = rho^2 * E0
Isotropic linear (unpenalized) interpolation E(rho) = rho * E0

items.entity: which porous unit defines the material (Table 2(a) vs Table 2(c))
items.description: Sec. 5.4 optimizes the beam twice: once with the natural-sample unit of Table 2(a) and once with the artificial unit of Table 2(c). The units appear only as images, and their different homogenized properties produce different density fields (Fig. 9(b), 9(c)). It is unclear which run a single-material re-run should reproduce.
readings: Reproduce the run with the Table 2(a) unit (result Fig. 9(b))
Reproduce the run with the Table 2(c) unit (result Fig. 9(c))
Run both, each with its own effective law

items.description: Eq. (27) bounds the density control coefficients by rho_min <= rho_ijk <= rho_max, the minimum and maximum relative densities of the porous unit. No values are given for Sec. 5.4. rho_min may be tied to the connectivity threshold c = 0 from Sec. 4.2.
readings: rho_min = 0.001, rho_max = 1.0 (standard solid-void bounds)
rho_min = 0.1, rho_max = 0.9
rho_min = 0.2, rho_max = 0.8
rho_min = unit's relative density at threshold c = 0 (connectivity limit), rho_max = 1.0

items.description: Sec. 4.3 represents rho as a B-spline with N_u x N_v x N_w control coefficients, which smooths the field. For the beam, neither the control-net size nor the degree is given, and no filter type or radius is stated. A structured-grid solver needs an equivalent filter.
readings: Coarse cubic B-spline density net (e.g. one coefficient per unit cell, ~20 x 8 x 8) evaluated at element centres
Density filter with radius ~1.5 elements
Density filter with radius ~ one unit-cell size (several elements)
No filter (element densities as design variables)

items.description: Sec. 4.3 solves equilibrium by isogeometric analysis (IGA) on a B-spline solid with N_e elements. The element count, knot spans and basis degree for the beam are not given, so the structured-grid resolution must be chosen.
readings: 60 x 24 x 24 hexahedra (2-mm cubes on 120x48x48)
120 x 48 x 48 hexahedra (1-mm cubes)
30 x 12 x 12 hexahedra (4-mm cubes)

items.entity: Optimality Criteria update and stopping rule
items.description: Sec. 4.3 says the problem is solved with Optimality Criteria (OC), but gives no move limit, damping exponent, convergence tolerance or iteration count.
readings: Move limit 0.2, damping eta = 0.5, stop when max density change < 0.01
Same update with a fixed number of iterations (e.g. 100)
